title: Circle-interval control of critical-density transfer times in totally ergodic countable abelian actions
source_title: Sets of transfer times with small densities
author: Michael Björklund; Alexander Fish; Ilya D. Shkredov
difficulty_reason: The cited compact action-set factor theorem and Kneser critical-pair theorem do not alone identify the original action's full transfer-time set or its endpoints. The author establishes a measurable transfer-time correspondence with a quantitative overshoot inequality and uses equality of the densities to recover the actual circle factor and sets. This additional correspondence shows precisely why only the two endpoint kernel cosets can differ from the inverse circle difference interval.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Countable discrete abelian G, standard probability space, totally ergodic measure-preserving action, positive-measure A,B with lower density equal to mu(A)+mu(B)<1. Density is along the finite sets satisfying the exact pointwise averaging condition1.1, not any arbitrary finite-set sequence or an assumed Folner restriction. Complete new transfer-time correspondence and overshoot argument preserved. Earlier Björklund–Fish action-set factor theorem and classical Kneser connected-group critical-pair theorem are explicit existing research foundations. Equality of the return set with the inverse circle difference interval is only modulo at most two kernel cosets; actual measure-positive interval transfer excludes endpoints. No semigroup extension, general nondensity criterion or parameter variant is separately counted. Source proof has mK(B) where mK(J) is intended in the stated correspondence inequality; adjacent Proposition2.7 and every subsequent equality explicitly use J.
